This is awesome! But if it's sending the Ethernet over the microUSB, won't that severely limit the possible bandwidth?
Not sure. I haven't seen an adapter like this before.

Not unless you have gigabit ethernet. USB 2 is 480 Mbit/s.

Frankly, if your home Internet is faster than that, I hate you and want you to suffer! :p

It's not about speed. It's about reliability. My Plex server never needs more than 15Mbps to send a full-HD movie, and most streaming services use less bandwidth than that. But, if you're 100 feet from your router, you might be getting a lot of buffering even though everything else in your network is really fast.

My Plex server always transcodes the video down. I believe that the chromecast only takes video with a bitrate of 10Mbps or less and the server always converts. Plex is the only reason I would consider getting this though, I would love to cut down on the transcoding.

Transcoding is heavily device dependent. Plex figures out what formats the device supports, and if it can stream it directly it does, and transcodes if it can't. It rarely needs to transcode to my Roku, but often does to my Chromecast or my PC. As long as your server's CPU can keep up with it, Plex shouldn't have to transcode "down," just "different" or at least not down enough to matter. 10Mbps should be plenty for anything, as Netflix only uses 5Mbps and looks fine for almost everything.

Correct, but frequently full 1080p files are much more than that and require transcoding. My server isn't the most glorious beast right now, it runs on an APU that I found in a bin of parts at the local computer shop which only does Intel so they didn't want it!

Mine's not much better. It's a 7-year-old dual-core Dell Optiplex. It can only transcode one program at a time, and if the bitrate is too high, it can't even manage one without lots of buffering. I've found that 1080p is not a guarantee of high quality. It could still have been ripped at a really low bitrate so it looks blocky even though the picture is technically 1920x1080.
With chromecast you pretty much will always need to transcode unless you get all your videos in like the single format CC supports.

It doesn't need to transcode for MP3, MKV (as long as the stream is h.264), AAC, and it can passthrough DTS and AC3. I'm pretty happy with the support although I wish it was a bit more of a swiss army knife so to speak.
